Anyone who sits in v/all/new knows there is a LOT of spam and self-promotion on Voat. Problem is that the "Spam" section of the user agreement is incredibly vague, which makes the line between the two blurry and enforcement subjective. I gave up on submitting to v/ReportSpammers because of it. One of the improvements I think could be made is having a ratio of self-promotion to overall submissions. On Reddit (boo hiss etc.), the unofficial number for this was 1 self-promoting submissions for every 9 submissions you had, or you were shadowbanned because you could have bought an ad instead.

I believe a similar stance would actually be beneficial to Voat. There are plenty of accounts that do nothing but promote their own content, and I think a rule like this would help stimulate content submission while allowing those who would like to self-promote contribute to the site in a non-monetary fashion. It would also greatly cut down on self-promoters posting the same submission to 3 or 4 subverses and hoping one sticks, forcing them to either pick the best fit or contribute more. The users of the site get more content and comments to peruse, the self-promoters that want to play ball can stay (I could finally stop downvoting them!), those who don't care about our community get a warning and then the boot. To me, this seems fair.

That said, Voat is a different website from Reddit and we should do things our own way here. I think 1/9 submissions might be too high a bar, for starters. Perhaps 1/4 submissions? Or possibly including comments for a higher amount, like 1/6 posts can be self-promotion?

What ideas and concerns do you guys have? Any ways this could be exploited? Do you think it might be against the idea of free speech on voat? I'm just bored and spitballing here, work with me!
How do we solve voat's self-promotion problem? An idea and hopefully discussion!

I enjoyed your post. I think most of the spam issues would become moot if the admins simply cleared out the spammers who've been reported at a regular clip (once a week at the very least). If they did, more people would feel energized to report them. That may be a game of whack-a-mole though.

Honestly, that's what I want too, but the first step is having clear rules in the User Agreement on spam. Having clear rules would allow Atko and Puttitout to either go through spammers with a checklist or even have publicly accountable (elected? limited term?) janitors to handle the "whack-a-mole" for them, given how much more useful those two would be improving the site's code base.
